text:
Marcus Reed: Quick one on baseline metrics: what are we calling TTFT for *streaming*? Right now I’m seeing 2 different numbers depending on whether we timestamp on server emit vs client receives first chunk. We need a single definition for Q1 baselines.

Nadia Rahman: +1, and it’s extra messy b/c first SSE "chunk" can contain multiple tokens (or partial token?) depending on flush behavior. If we define TTFT as "first token arrives at client" it’s not stable across network and buffering.

Logan Wright: From telemetry POV we can reliably capture:
- t_request_received (server)
- t_first_token_generated (server)
- t_first_chunk_written (server)
Client-side "received" is only available in SDKs and uses wall clock (NTP drift), plus proxies.

Jonas Weber: For baselines we need something reproducible and comparable across regions/hardware. My vote: TTFT = time from server recv -> first token *generated* (or first token *enqueued for send*). Then separately report "time to first byte" as an E2E-ish metric.

Sofia Ivanova: Scheduling angle: "first token generated" includes queue wait + prefill + first decode step. That’s what we want to optimize. "first chunk written" adds network flush + streaming aggregation behavior (which can change if we tweak chunk size).

Sean Gallagher: SRE hat: if we bake network into TTFT baseline, p95/p99 will be noisy and we’ll chase ghosts (load balancer, kernel jitter, etc). But product folks care about user-perceived speed. Can we carry both?

Marcus Reed: ok so propose:
1) `ttft_server_ms` = t_first_token_generated - t_request_received
2) `ttfb_server_ms` (or `ttft_wire_ms`) = t_first_chunk_written - t_request_received
3) optional `ttft_client_ms` in SDK harness only
Does that line up with Console + dashboards?

Logan Wright: We can emit (1) + (2) from runtime, yes. Need to be careful on what counts as "first token" for streaming:
- if we do any token buffering before first emit, `first_chunk_written` can jump.
- but `first_token_generated` should be the first decode token completion.

Nadia Rahman: Another edge: some routes send a "role": "assistant" prelude event before tokens. That should *not* count. TTFT should start at request and end at first actual generated token. Otherwise you can get TTFT ~= 0.

Rina Kobayashi: In the runner I can add a sanity check that the first streaming event with tokens is the one we use for client measurement. But server-side metric shouldn’t depend on SSE framing.

Jonas Weber: Suggest we codify in methodology doc:
- TTFT (baseline) = server monotonic clock, first decode token generated
- add separate metric: "time to first stream byte" for end-to-end-ish
- for client comparisons, we do a controlled harness in same region/VPC to validate drift, but don’t gate on it.

Sofia Ivanova: :thumbsup: also need to define what happens if model returns empty output / tool call with no tokens. For baseline runs we can constrain workloads to produce >= 1 token.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Also please call out that `ttft_server_ms` should use monotonic clock, not wall. We’ve been burned there.

Logan Wright: Re "first-token chunking": current instrumentation in streaming path records "first chunk" at the time we enqueue to the HTTP writer, but we sometimes buffer until we have N bytes. So `ttfb` will reflect that buffer setting.

Nadia Rahman: Which is fine if we’re explicit. The worry is folks will look at TTFT and assume it’s user-perceived. We should name it clearly (server-side).

Marcus Reed: Naming: `ttft_server_ms` + `ttft_client_ms`? and `ttfb_server_ms`? (I don’t love TTFT twice)

Jonas Weber: Maybe:
- `ttft_ms` reserved for server-side baseline metric
- `ttfb_ms` for first byte/chunk
- `ttft_client_ms` only in harness artifacts
but we should be consistent across docs/Console.

Logan Wright: Works if we’re disciplined. But Console currently labels TTFT from the server timestamp (first token generated). We should verify it matches what SDK sees, at least under controlled conditions.

Nadia Rahman: That’s the core issue. I’ve seen cases where Console TTFT is 150ms but client sees 400-500ms. Could be buffering, could be timestamp bug.

Sean Gallagher: Action item: telemetry validation harness. Compare runtime timestamps vs client-measured timings for streaming + non-streaming, across a couple traffic shapes. If mismatch > X% we flag.

Rina Kobayashi: I can add this to benchmark-lab runner as an optional mode: run N requests, capture client-side timers + server metrics from response headers, output diff summary.

Marcus Reed: Great. I’ll file a Linear for this so we can track + get sign-off from Telemetry/Obs.

Marcus Reed: (filed) ENG-4832 "Add TTFT/TPOT telemetry validation harness". Assigning myself + tagging @Logan Wright @Nadia Rahman @Rina Kobayashi @Jonas Weber. Goal: confirm TTFT/TPOT definitions for streaming, catch first-chunk edge cases.

Logan Wright: :thumbsup: I’ll add notes on what headers/fields we can expose in response metadata to make harness easier.

Nadia Rahman: :eyes: I’ll dig into the streaming instrumentation path. I suspect we’re setting first-token timestamp on "first delta event" not "first token" in one codepath.

Sofia Ivanova: Once definitions are locked, please update the baseline methodology doc + the workload suite spec so we don’t end up mixing metrics across runs.

Jonas Weber: +1 and we should call out explicitly in baselines: TTFT is server-side and not a user-perceived SLO. Otherwise this will get misused.

Sean Gallagher: Cool. When ENG-4832 lands, SRE can set variance budgets on `ttft_ms` and treat `ttfb_ms` as informational (unless it explodes).

Marcus Reed: 👍 I’ll also ping Henry/Paula once we settle naming, since customer-facing transparency will care about which number we publish.
